			<font style="display:inline;">The Company has valued the acquired assets and liabilities based on their fair value. The fair values included in the balance sheet as of </font><font style="display:inline;">December&nbsp;31, 2015</font><font style="display:inline;"> are based on the best estimates of management. At </font><font style="display:inline;">December&nbsp;31, 2015</font><font style="display:inline;"> the allocation of the purchase price has been finalized, including the estimated useful lives and related amortization of acquired assets. </font>

			<font style="display:inline;">The difference between the total consideration and the fair value of the net assets acquired of $</font><font style="display:inline;">315.4</font><font style="display:inline;"> million was recorded to goodwill in the consolidated balance sheet. Goodwill represents the excess of the purchase price over the fair value of the tangible and identifiable intangible assets acquired and liabilities assumed, principally representing certain ope</font><font style="display:inline;">rational synergies. The majority of the acquired intangibles and goodwill are expected to be deductible for tax purposes.&nbsp; </font><font style="display:inline;">As a result of the measurement period adjustments described above, goodwill decreased from </font><font style="display:inline;">$12.5</font><font style="display:inline;"> million as of March 31, 2015 to $9.6 million as of December 31, 2015.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:1pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;">In accordance with the relevant accounting guidance, goodwill is not amortized. However, it must be assessed for impairment using fair value measurement techniques on an annual basis or more frequently if facts and circumstances warrant such a review. All goodwill has been assigned to the Company&#x2019;s single reporting unit, which is the single operating segment by which the chief operating decision maker manages the Company. For purposes of assessing the impairment of goodwill, the Company uses its market capitalization as an input to its determination of fair value. If the carrying amount of the net assets of the Company exceeds the fair value, then a goodwill impairment test is performed to measure the amount of the impairment loss, if any.&nbsp;&nbsp;Although there have been no indicators of impairment to date with respect to the Company&#x2019;s goodwill and long-lived intangible assets, the Company may need to assess these assets for impairment in the future based on the outcome of the ongoing investigations of the SEC and Department of Justice (Note 9), which could have a material adverse effect on the Company&#x2019;s business. </font>

			<font style="display:inline;">The significant increase in the inventory balance as of </font><font style="display:inline;">December&nbsp;31, 2015</font><font style="display:inline;"> is related to the fair value of metreleptin inventory from the acquisition of MYALEPT, as described in Note 3.&nbsp;&nbsp;During the </font><font style="display:inline;">years ended December&nbsp;31, 2015, 2014 and 2013</font><font style="display:inline;">, the Company recorded charges in the consolidated statement of operations for excess </font><font style="display:inline;">and obsolete </font><font style="display:inline;">inventory of $</font><font style="display:inline;">2.5</font><font style="display:inline;"> million</font><font style="display:inline;">,</font><font style="display:inline;"> $1.5 million</font><font style="display:inline;"> and $0.2 million</font><font style="display:inline;">, respectively. </font>

			<font style="display:inline;font-size:1pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 1pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:1pt;">&nbsp;</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">6. Fair Value of Financial Instruments </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:6pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Fair value is defined as the exchange price that would be received for an asset or paid to transfer a liability (an exit price) in the principal or most advantageous market for the asset or liability in an orderly transaction between market participants at the measurement date. ASC 820, </font><font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;">Fair Value Measurements and Disclosures</font><font style="display:inline;"> established a fair value hierarchy for those instruments measured at fair value that distinguishes between fair value measurements based on market data (observable inputs) and those based on the Company&#x2019;s own assumptions (unobservable inputs). This hierarchy maximizes the use of observable inputs and minimizes the use of unobservable inputs. The three levels of inputs used to measure fair value are as follows: </font>
		</p>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:24pt;"><p style="width:24pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 18.00pt; display: inline;">
			<p style="border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;">
				<font style="margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;font-family:Symbol;font-size:10pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9;;"> &#xB7;</font>
			</p>
		</td><td style="width:0pt;"><p style="width:0pt;width:0pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Level 1</font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;">&#x2014;Quoted prices in active markets for identical assets or liabilities that the Company has the ability to access at the measurement date. The Company&#x2019;s Level 1 assets consist of cash and money market investments. </font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:24pt;"><p style="width:24pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 18.00pt; display: inline;">
			<p style="border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;">
				<font style="margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;font-family:Symbol;font-size:10pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9;;"> &#xB7;</font>
			</p>
		</td><td style="width:0pt;"><p style="width:0pt;width:0pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Level 2</font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;">&#x2014;Inputs other than quoted prices in active markets that are observable for the asset or liability, either directly or indirectly. The Company&#x2019;s Level 2 assets consist of corporate debt securities and commercial paper. </font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:24pt;"><p style="width:24pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 18.00pt; display: inline;">
			<p style="border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;">
				<font style="margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;font-family:Symbol;font-size:10pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9;;"> &#xB7;</font>
			</p>
		</td><td style="width:0pt;"><p style="width:0pt;width:0pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">

Interest is payable semi-annually in arrears on February&nbsp;15 and August&nbsp;15 of each year, beginning on February&nbsp;15, 2015.</font><font style="display:inline;"> The Company separately accounted for the liability and equity components of the Convertible Notes by allocating the proceeds between the liability component and equity component, as further discussed in Note 10. The estimated fair value of the Convertible Notes at </font><font style="display:inline;">December&nbsp;31, 2015</font><font style="display:inline;"> was </font><font style="display:inline;">$</font><font style="display:inline;">215.2</font><font style="display:inline;"> million.</font><font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>

			<font style="display:inline;">Rent expense under operating leases was approximately $</font><font style="display:inline;">4.6</font><font style="display:inline;"> million, </font><font style="display:inline;">$3.2</font><font style="display:inline;"> million and </font><font style="display:inline;">$1.2</font><font style="display:inline;"> million for the </font><font style="display:inline;">years ended December&nbsp;31, 2015, 2014 and 2013</font><font style="display:inline;">, respectively. </font>

			<font style="display:inline;">On November&nbsp;24, 2010, the Company entered into a lease for office space in Bedminster, New Jersey. The lease provided for an initial base rent of </font><font style="display:inline;">$12,000</font><font style="display:inline;"> per month plus certain operating expenses and taxes beginning on April&nbsp;1, 2011, and increased on an annual basis beginning in April 2012. As discussed in Note 17, the Company has closed this facility and, in January 2012, entered into an agreement to sublease this facility. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Effective January&nbsp;1, 2011, the Company entered into a five year lease for office space for its headquarters in Cambridge, Massachusetts, with RREEF America REIT II Corp. PPP, (&#x201C;RREEF&#x201D;) and amended this lease in November 2011. On September&nbsp;24, 2012, the Company entered into a second amendment to lease additional square footage which provided for an increase in base rent beginning February&nbsp;1, 2013. On June&nbsp;28, 2013, the Company entered into a third amendment to lease additional square footage which provided for an increase in base rent beginning August&nbsp;31, 2013. On January&nbsp;9, 2014, the Company entered into its fourth lease amendment to lease additional square footage which provided for an escalation of rent payments of approximately </font><font style="display:inline;">$0.2</font><font style="display:inline;"> million a month resulting in an increase in base rent beginning in May&nbsp;1, 2014, a tenant improvement allowance of approximately </font><font style="display:inline;">$0.8</font><font style="display:inline;"> million and as well as extend the expiration date for all of the space the Company leases from RREEF from </font><font style="display:inline;">August&nbsp;31, 2017</font><font style="display:inline;"> to </font><font style="display:inline;">April&nbsp;30, 2019</font><font style="display:inline;">. In addition to the base rent, the Company is responsible for its share of operating expenses and real estate taxes. In May 2014, the Company exercised an expansion option under the first amendment to lease additional square footage which provided for an increase in base rent beginning on April 1, 2015. </font>

If the Company&#x2019;s activities in Brazil are found to violate any laws or any other governmental regulations, it may be subject to: significant civil and administrative penalties imposed by Brazilian regulatory authorities, damages and fines, suspension of its social rights before Interfarma, and/or exclusion of the its membership in Interfarma. Under certain circumstances, the Company could be barred from further named patient sales in Brazil for lomitapide and/or metreleptin due to penalties imposed by Brazilian regulatory authorities or through civil actions initiated by federal, state, or municipal public prosecutors.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, the Company believes the investigations in Brazil have contributed to a slower turn-around between price quotation and orders, including re-orders, from the federal government, and, in some cases, delays in orders and re-orders from the government of S&#xE3;o Paulo after a patient has obtained access to JUXTAPID through the judicial process. These delays may continue, and the Company may experience other delays or suspension of the ordering process. Similarly, the Company has faced, and may continue to face, a reluctance of physicians to prescribe JUXTAPID, and some patients to take or stay on JUXTAPID, while the investigations are ongoing, particularly given that the investigators in Brazil have recently made formal inquiries of certain prescribers of lomitapide and there has been local media coverage of such inquiries and its activities in Brazil. Recently, the Company has observed an increase in the drop-out rate of patients on JUXTAPID in Brazil, and it believes that part of the reason for the increase is due to the investigations. These issues could negatively affect the Company&#x2019;s ability to generate product revenue consistent with its expectations, and may impact its ability to achieve and maintain profitability or maintain cash-flow-positive operations. Prescriptions for and sales of metreleptin in Brazil may also be negatively affected.&nbsp;&nbsp;As of the filing date of this 10-K, the Company cannot determine if a loss is probable as a result of the investigations in Brazil and whether the outcome will </font><font style="display:inline;"></font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">

		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">In January&nbsp;2014, a putative class action lawsuit was filed against the Company and certain of its executive officers in the United States District Court for the District of Massachusetts alleging certain misstatements and omissions related to the marketing of JUXTAPID and the Company&#x2019;s financial performance in violation of the federal securities laws. On March&nbsp;11, 2015, the Court appointed co-lead plaintiffs and lead counsel. On April&nbsp;1, 2015, the Court entered an order permitting and setting a schedule for co-lead plaintiffs to file an amended complaint within </font><font style="display:inline;">60</font><font style="display:inline;"> days, and for defendants to file responsive pleadings, co-lead plaintiffs to file any opposition, and defendants to file reply briefs. Accordingly, co-lead plaintiffs filed an amended complaint on June&nbsp;1, 2015.&nbsp;The amended complaint filed against the Company and certain of its former executive officers alleges that defendants made certain misstatements and omissions during the first three quarters&nbsp;of 2014 related to the Company&#x2019;s revenue projections for JUXTAPID for 2014, as well as data underlying those projections, in violation of the federal securities laws.&nbsp;The Company filed a motion to dismiss the amended complaint for failure to state a claim on July&nbsp;31, 2015. &nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;">On August 21, 2015, co-lead plaintiffs filed a putative second amended complaint, which alleges that the defendants made certain misstatements and omissions from April 2013 through October 2014 related to the marketing of JUXTAPID and the Company&#x2019;s financial projections, as well as data underlying those projections.&nbsp;&nbsp;On September 4, 2015, the Company moved to strike the second amended complaint for the co-lead plaintiffs&#x2019; failure to seek leave of court to file a second amended pleading, and briefing is complete with respect to the motion to strike.</font><font style="display:inline;"> &nbsp; &nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;">Oral argument on the motion to strike was held on March 9, 2016 and continued to April 7, 2016.&nbsp; </font><font style="display:inline;">As of the filing date of this 10-K, the Company cannot determine if a loss is probable as a result of the class action lawsuit and whether the outcome will have a material adverse effect on its business and, as a result, the Company has not recorded any amounts for a loss contingency.</font><font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>

			<font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;">Term Loan </font>

			<font style="display:inline;">On March&nbsp;28, 2012, the Company entered into a Loan and Security Agreement (as amended the &#x201C;Loan and Security Agreement&#x201D;) with Silicon Valley Bank, pursuant to which Silicon Valley Bank made a term loan to the Company in the principal amount of </font><font style="display:inline;">$10.0</font><font style="display:inline;"> million (the &#x201C;2012 Term Loan Advance&#x201D;). (collectively, &#x201C;the Hercules Funds&#x201D;). </font>

The indenture contains customary terms and covenants and events of default. If an event of default (other than certain events of bankruptcy, insolvency or reorganization involving the Company) occurs and is continuing, the Trustee by notice to the Company, or the holders of at least </font><font style="display:inline;">25%</font><font style="display:inline;"> in principal amount of the outstanding Convertible Notes by written notice to the Company and the Trustee, may declare </font><font style="display:inline;">100%</font><font style="display:inline;"> of the principal of and accrued and unpaid interest, if any, on all of the Convertible Notes to be due and payable. Upon such a declaration of acceleration, such principal and accrued and unpaid interest, if any, will be due and payable immediately. Upon the occurrence of certain events of bankruptcy, insolvency or reorganization involving the Company, </font><font style="display:inline;">100%</font><font style="display:inline;"> of the principal and accrued and unpaid interest, if any, on the Convertible Notes will become due and payable automatically. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the indenture provides that, upon the Company&#x2019;s election, and for up to </font><font style="display:inline;">180</font><font style="display:inline;"> days, the sole remedy for an event of default relating to certain failures by the Company to comply with certain reporting covenants in the indenture consists exclusively of the right to receive additional interest on the Convertible Notes.&nbsp;&nbsp;If Silicon Valley Bank elects to accelerate the principal amount due under the Loan and Security Agreement and the Company fails to pay such amount, the Trustee or holders of at least 25% of the aggregate principal amount of the Notes may deliver a notice of default to the Company. The Company&#x2019;s failure to pay the amount due under the Loan and Security Agreement within </font><font style="display:inline;">30</font><font style="display:inline;"> days following its receipt of such notice would be deemed an event of default under the Indenture and, among other remedies, the Trustee or holders of at least 25% of the aggregate principal amount of the Notes could declare all unpaid principal of the Notes immediately due and payable.&nbsp; </font><font style="display:inline;">The default provision, which applies to the failure to repay the outstanding 2015 Term Loan Advance, or other indebtedness, is not considered probable to </font><font style="display:inline;"></font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;">150</font><font style="display:inline;"></font><font style="display:inline;"></font><font style="display:inline;"></font><font style="display:inline;"></font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><hr align="center" style='background-color:#000000; border-width:0; color:#000000; height:2pt; lineheight:0; width:100%;'></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 30pt;color:#0563C1;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:12pt 0pt 0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;">occur as the Company has sufficient capital to repay the outstanding obligations under the Loan and Security Agreement if such amounts are accelerated by Silicon Valley Bank.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">In accordance with accounting guidance for debt with conversion and other options, the Company separately accounted for the liability and equity components of the Convertible Notes by allocating the proceeds between the liability component and the embedded conversion option, or equity component, due to the Company&#x2019;s ability to settle the Convertible Notes in cash, common stock, or a combination of cash and common stock at the option of the Company. The carrying amount of the liability component was calculated by measuring the fair value of a similar liability that does not have an associated convertible feature. The allocation was performed in a manner that reflected the Company&#x2019;s non-convertible debt borrowing rate for similar debt. The equity component of the Convertible Notes was recognized as a debt discount and represents the difference between the gross proceeds from the issuance of the Convertible Notes and the fair value of the liability of the Convertible Notes on their respective dates of issuance. The excess of the principal amount of the liability component over its carrying amount, or debt discount, is amortized to interest expense using the effective interest method over </font><font style="display:inline;">five</font><font style="display:inline;"> years, or the life of the Convertible Notes. The equity component is not remeasured as long as it continues to meet the conditions for equity classification. </font>
		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;">Convertible Bond Hedge and Warrant Transactions </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:6pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">In connection with the offering of the Convertible Notes and in order to reduce the potential dilution to the Company&#x2019;s common stock and/or offset cash payments due upon conversion of the Convertible Notes, the Company entered into convertible bond hedge transactions convertible into approximately </font><font style="display:inline;">7.9</font><font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;million shares of the Company&#x2019;s common stock (or the value thereof), subject to adjustment, underlying the </font><font style="display:inline;">$325.0</font><font style="display:inline;"> million aggregate principal amount of the Convertible Notes. The convertible bond hedges have an exercise price of approximately </font><font style="display:inline;">$41.175</font><font style="display:inline;"> per share, subject to adjustment upon certain events, and are exercisable when and if the Convertible Notes are converted. If upon conversion of the Convertible Notes, the price of the Company&#x2019;s common stock is above the exercise price of the convertible bond hedges, shares of the Company&#x2019;s common stock and/or cash will be delivered with an aggregate value approximately equal to the difference between the price of the Company&#x2019;s common stock at the conversion date and the exercise price, multiplied by the number of shares of the Company&#x2019;s common stock related to the convertible bond hedges being exercised. The convertible bond hedges are separate transactions entered into by the Company and are not part of the terms of the Convertible Notes or the warrants, discussed below. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:9pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">At the same time, the Company also entered into separate warrant transactions relating to, in the aggregate, approximately </font><font style="display:inline;">7.9</font><font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;million shares of the Company&#x2019;s common stock, subject to customary adjustments but capped at a maximum of approximately </font><font style="display:inline;">15.8</font><font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;million shares of the Company&#x2019;s common stock underlying the </font><font style="display:inline;">$325.0</font><font style="display:inline;"> million aggregate principal amount of the Convertible Notes. The initial exercise price of the warrants is </font><font style="display:inline;">$53.375</font><font style="display:inline;"> per share, subject to adjustment upon certain events. The warrants would separately have a dilutive effect to the extent that the market value per share of the Company&#x2019;s common stock, as measured under the terms of the warrants, exceeds the applicable exercise price of the warrants. The Company received </font><font style="display:inline;">$60.5</font><font style="display:inline;"> million for these warrants and recorded this amount to additional paid-in capital. </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:1pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">11. Basic and Diluted Net Loss per Common Share </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:6pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Basic net loss per common share is calculated by dividing the net loss by the weighted-average number of common shares outstanding for the period. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">In August&nbsp;2014, in connection with the issuance of the Convertible Notes, the Company entered into convertible bond hedges. The convertible bond hedges are not included for purposes of calculating the number of diluted shares outstanding, as their effect would be anti-dilutive. The convertible bond hedges are generally expected, but not guaranteed, to reduce the potential dilution upon conversion of the Convertible Notes. See Note 10, &#x201C;Debt Financing&#x201D; for additional information. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Diluted net loss per common share is computed by dividing the net loss by the weighted-average number of unrestricted common shares and dilutive common share equivalents outstanding for the period, determined using the treasury-stock and if-converted methods. Since the Company has had net losses for all periods presented, all potentially dilutive securities are anti-dilutive. Accordingly, basic and diluted net loss per common share are equal. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:1pt;"></font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;">152</font><font style="display:inline;"></font><font style="display:inline;"></font><font style="display:inline;"></font><font style="display:inline;"></font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><hr align="center" style='background-color:#000000; border-width:0; color:#000000; height:2pt; lineheight:0; width:100%;'></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><div style="width:100%">

Each holder of common stock is entitled to vote on all matters and is entitled to </font><font style="display:inline;">one</font><font style="display:inline;"> vote for each share held. </font>

		<p style="margin:13.5pt 0pt 0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">13. Stock Option Plans </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company issues stock options, restricted stock and restricted stock units (&#x201C;RSUs&#x201D;) with service conditions, which are generally the vesting periods of the awards. The Company has issued stock options and RSUs that vest upon the satisfaction of certain performance conditions. The Company also has issued stock options and RSUs that vest upon the satisfaction of certain market conditions. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:9pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company&#x2019;s 2010 Stock Option and Incentive Plan (the &#x201C;2010 Option Plan&#x201D;) was approved by stockholders in </font><font style="display:inline;">October 2010</font><font style="display:inline;">. The 2010 Option Plan allows the Company to make grants of incentive stock options, non-qualified stock </font><font style="display:inline;"></font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;">153</font><font style="display:inline;"></font><font style="display:inline;"></font><font style="display:inline;"></font><font style="display:inline;"></font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><hr align="center" style='background-color:#000000; border-width:0; color:#000000; height:2pt; lineheight:0; width:100%;'></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 30pt;color:#0563C1;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:9pt 0pt 0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;">options, stock appreciation rights, restricted stock awards, restricted stock units, unrestricted stock awards, cash-based awards, performance share awards and dividend equivalent rights. All full-time and part-time officers, employees, non-employee directors and other key persons, including consultants and prospective employees, are eligible to participate in the 2010 Option Plan. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:9pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">There are certain limits on the number of awards that may be granted under the 2010 Option Plan. For example, no more than </font><font style="display:inline;">1,500,000</font><font style="display:inline;"> shares of common stock may be granted in the form of stock options or stock appreciation rights to any one individual during any one-calendar-year period. Annually on January&nbsp;1, the maximum number of shares available for issuance under the 2010 Option Plan increases by </font><font style="display:inline;">4%</font><font style="display:inline;"> of the number of shares of Common Stock issued and outstanding on the immediately preceding December&nbsp;31. At </font><font style="display:inline;">December&nbsp;31, 2015</font><font style="display:inline;">, the Company has </font><font style="display:inline;">945,576</font><font style="display:inline;"> shares of common stock available for issuance under its 2010</font><font style="display:inline;"> Option Plan.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:9pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">In October 2012, the Compensation Committee of the Company&#x2019;s Board of Directors approved the reservation of </font><font style="display:inline;">1,000,000</font><font style="display:inline;"> shares of common stock to be used exclusively for the grant of non-qualified stock options to individuals who were not previously an employee or non-employee of the Company as an inducement new hire stock option award. These options are granted under the Company&#x2019;s 2012 Inducement Stock Option Plan (the &#x201C;2012 Option Plan&#x201D;). In October 2013, the Compensation Committee of the Company&#x2019;s Board of Directors approved an amendment to the 2012 Option Plan to reserve an additional </font><font style="display:inline;">1,000,000</font><font style="display:inline;"> shares of common stock for which the additional shares are only available for grant until December&nbsp;31, 2014. Then, in December 2014, the Compensation Committee of the Company&#x2019;s Board of Directors approved an amendment to the 2012 Option Plan to reserve an additional </font><font style="display:inline;">750,000</font><font style="display:inline;"> shares of common stock and extend the time period for the usage of the remaining reserve of common stock until </font><font style="display:inline;">December&nbsp;31, 2015</font><font style="display:inline;">. At </font><font style="display:inline;">December&nbsp;31, 2015</font><font style="display:inline;">, the Company has </font><font style="display:inline;">1,229,053</font><font style="display:inline;"> shares of common stock available for issuance under the 2012 Option Plan. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:9pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The 2010 Option Plan and 2012 Option Plan are administered by the Compensation Committee (&#x201C;the administrator&#x201D;). Subject to the terms of the plans and applicable laws and regulations, the administrator has full power and authority to select the participants to whom awards will be granted, to make any combination of awards to participants, to delegate authority to make awards, to accelerate the exercisability or vesting of any award and to determine the specific terms and conditions of each award. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:9pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The exercise price of stock options awarded under the 2010 and 2012 Option Plans may not be less than the fair value of the Company&#x2019;s common stock on the date of the option grant, and the term of each option may not exceed </font><font style="display:inline;">ten</font><font style="display:inline;"> years from the date of grant. The administrator will determine at what time or times each option may be exercised and, subject to the provisions of the 2010 Option Plan and 2012 Option Plan, the period of time, if any, after retirement, death, disability or other termination of employment during which options may be exercised. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:9pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">In the event of a merger, sale or dissolution, or a similar sale event, unless assumed or substituted, all stock options and restricted stock awards granted under all of the Company&#x2019;s stock option plans that are not exercisable immediately prior to the effective time of a sale event will automatically become fully exercisable, and non-forfeitable and awards with conditions and restrictions relating to the attainment of performance goals may become vested and non-forfeitable in connection with a sale event in the administrator&#x2019;s discretion. In addition, upon the effective time of any such sale event, the Company&#x2019;s stock option plans and all awards will terminate unless the parties to the transaction, in their discretion, provide for appropriate substitutions or assumptions of outstanding awards. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:13.5pt 0pt 0pt 12.2pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Determining the Fair Value of Stock Awards and Restricted Stock Unit Awards </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt 12.2pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Stock Options </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company measures the fair value of stock options with service-based and performance-based vesting criteria to employees, consultants and directors on the date of grant using the Black Scholes option pricing model. The fair value of equity instruments issued to non-employees is remeasured as the award vests. For awards that vest upon the achievement of a market condition, the Company calculates the estimated fair value of the stock-based awards using a Monte Carlo simulation. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:9pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company does not have sufficient history to support a calculation of volatility and expected term using only its historical data. As such, the Company has used a weighted-average volatility considering the Company&#x2019;s own volatility since its initial public offering in October 2010 and the volatilities of several guideline companies. For </font><font style="display:inline;"></font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;">154</font><font style="display:inline;"></font><font style="display:inline;"></font><font style="display:inline;"></font><font style="display:inline;"></font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:9pt 0pt 0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;">purposes of identifying similar entities, the Company considered characteristics such as industry, length of trading history, and stage of life cycle. In 2014, in light of the commercial status of the Company, the Company revised the guideline companies that it utilizes as an input in calculating the weighted average method, resulting in a significant change in the volatility input from the prior years. The assumed dividend yield was based on the Company&#x2019;s expectation of not paying dividends in the foreseeable future. The average expected life was determined according to the &#x201C;simplified method&#x201D; as described in SAB 110, which is the mid-point between the vesting date and the end of the contractual term. The risk-free interest rate is determined by reference to implied yields available from U.S. Treasury securities with a remaining term equal to the expected life assumed at the date of grant. Forfeitures are estimated based on the Company&#x2019;s historical analysis of both options and awards that forfeited prior to vesting. The weighted average-grant date fair values of stock options granted during the </font><font style="display:inline;">years ended December&nbsp;31, 2015, 2014 and 2013 </font><font style="display:inline;">were $</font><font style="display:inline;">12.22</font><font style="display:inline;">, &nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;">$25.02</font><font style="display:inline;">, and </font><font style="display:inline;">$31.79</font><font style="display:inline;">, respectively. The weighted-average assumptions used in the Black-Scholes option-pricing model are as follows: </font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 12.25pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Restricted Stock Unit Awards (RSUs) </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:6pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">RSUs are generally subject to forfeiture if employment terminates prior to the release of vesting restrictions. The Company expenses the cost of the RSUs with service-based vesting conditions, which is determined to be the fair value of the shares of common stock underlying the RSUs at the date of grant, ratably over the period during which the vesting restrictions lapse. Additionally, the Company grants RSUs that vest upon the achievement of a market condition. The fair value of RSUs with market-based vesting conditions is determined using a Monte Carlo simulation and the Company recognizes compensation expense over the derived service period. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:9pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

In accordance with SEC Staff Accounting Bulletin (&#x201C;SAB&#x201D;) No.&nbsp;99, Materiality and SAB No.&nbsp;108 (&#x201C;SAB 108&#x201D;), Considering the Effects of Prior Year Misstatements when Quantifying Misstatements in Current Year Financial Statements, the Company assessed the materiality of this error on its financial statements for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013, using both the roll-over method and iron-curtain methods as defined in SAB 108. 			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">14. Employee Benefit Plan </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company maintains a defined contribution 401(k) plan (the &#x201C;Plan&#x201D;) in which substantially all of its permanent U.S. employees are eligible to participate. The Company makes matching contributions of </font><font style="display:inline;">50%</font><font style="display:inline;"> of the first </font><font style="display:inline;">6%</font><font style="display:inline;"> of employees&#x2019; contributions to the Plan. The federal NOL carryforwards expire at various dates from </font><font style="display:inline;">2025</font><font style="display:inline;"> through </font><font style="display:inline;">2035</font><font style="display:inline;">, if not utilized. 			<font style="display:inline;">The Company believes a change of ownership within the meaning of Section&nbsp;382 and 383 of the Internal Revenue Code occurred in 2005 and 2012. Under Section&nbsp;382 and 383 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended, if a corporation undergoes an &#x201C;ownership change,&#x201D; generally defined as a greater than 50% change (by value) in its equity ownership over a three-year period, the corporation&#x2019;s ability to use its pre-change net operating loss carryforwards, or NOLs, and other pre-change tax attributes (such as research tax credits) to offset its post-change income may be limited. As a result, the Company&#x2019;s U.S. federal net operating loss and general business credit utilization will be limited to an amount equal to the market capitalization at the time of the ownership change multiplied by the federal long-term tax exempt rate. </font>

			<font style="display:inline;">In the quarter ended March&nbsp;31, 2014, the Company migrated from its legacy third</font><font style="display:inline;">-</font><font style="display:inline;">party stock option software application to a new third</font><font style="display:inline;">-</font><font style="display:inline;">party software application and noted a significant cumulative difference in the manner in which the two systems calculated stock-based compensation expense for service type awards granted to employees since 2010, which the Company concluded was an error in its historical stock-based compensation expense. The Company assessed the impact of the difference between the stock-based compensation expense as</font><font style="display:inline;"> calculated by the legacy third-</font><font style="display:inline;">party stock op</font><font style="display:inline;">tion software and the new third-</font><font style="display:inline;">party software and as a result of the analysis, recorded an additional $1.5 million in stock-based compensation expense to correct the error related to the incorrect calculation of service type awards to employees in its consolidated statement of operations in the quarter ending March&nbsp;31, 2014. In accordance with SEC Staff Accounting Bulletin (&#x201C;SAB&#x201D;) No.&nbsp;99, </font><font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;">Materiality</font><font style="display:inline;"> and SAB No.&nbsp;108 (&#x201C;SAB 108&#x201D;), </font><font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;">Considering the Effects of Prior Year Misstatements when Quantifying Misstatements in Current Year Financial Statements</font><font style="display:inline;">, the Company assessed the materiality of this error on its financial statements for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013, using both the roll-over method and iron-curtain methods as defined in SAB 108. The Company concluded the effect of this error was not material to its financial statements for any prior period and, as such, those financial statements are not materially misstated. The Company also concluded that providing for the correction of the error in 2014 did not have a material effect on its financial statements for the quarter ended March&nbsp;31, 2014 and year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014. </font>
		</p>

			<font style="display:inline;">In preparing its financial statements for the quarter ended June 30, 2015, the Company determined that its accounting related to the elimination of intercompany profits attributable to sales of inventory between consolidated subsidiaries, including the associated exchange rate effect on these transactions, was not corr</font><font style="display:inline;">ect. The error</font><font style="display:inline;"> primarily affected cost of product sales and accumulated other comprehensive income and loss accounts, with a lesser effect on its inventory, which was corrected by the Company in the second quarter of 2015. The Company determined the effect of the error to be an understatement of cost of product sales of approximately </font><font style="display:inline;">$1.7</font><font style="display:inline;"> million for the year ended December 31, 2014 and an overstatement of cost of product sales of approximately </font><font style="display:inline;">$0.6</font><font style="display:inline;"> million for the three months ended March 31, 2015. Cost of product sales in the three months ended June 30, 2015 includes </font><font style="display:inline;">$1.1</font><font style="display:inline;"> million related to this error. In accordance with SAB No.&nbsp;99, </font><font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;">Materiality</font><font style="display:inline;"> and SAB 108, </font><font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;">Considering the Effects of Prior Year Misstatements when Quantifying Misstatements in Current Year Financial Statements</font><font style="display:inline;">, the Company assessed the materiality of this error on its financial statements for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 and for the three months ended March 31, 2015, using both the roll-over method and iron-curtain methods as defined in SAB 108. The Company concluded the effect of this error was not material to its financial statements for any prior period and, as such, those financial statements are not materially misstated.</font>

			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">Item&nbsp; 9A.</font><font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;;font-size: 10pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;padding:0pt 28pt 0pt 0pt;"></font><font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">Controls and Procedure</font><a name="ControlsandProcedures_115380"></a><font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">s. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:3pt 0pt 0pt 12.25pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Disclosure Controls and Procedures </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:3pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Our management, with the participation of our principal executive officer and our principal financial officer, evaluated, as of the end of the period covered by this Annual Report on Form 10-K, the effectiveness of our disclosure controls and procedures. Based on that evaluation, our principal executive officer and principal financial officer concluded that our disclosure controls and procedures as of such date are not effective due to material weaknesses in our controls over the financial reporting process related to business combinations and accounting for significant </font><font style="display:inline;">non-routine</font><font style="display:inline;"> transactions.&nbsp;&nbsp;Disclosure controls and procedures include, without limitation, controls and procedures designed to ensure that information required to be disclosed by us in the reports we file or submit under the Exchange Act is accumulated and communicated to our management, including our principal executive officer and principal financial officer, as appropriate to allow timely decisions regarding required disclosure. Based upon that evaluation, our principal executive officer and principal financial officer concluded that our disclosure controls and procedures were not effective at </font><font style="display:inline;">December&nbsp;31, 2015</font><font style="display:inline;">. &nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:9pt 0pt 0pt 12.25pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Management&#x2019;s Report on Internal Control over Financial Reporting </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:3pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Our management is responsible for establishing and maintaining adequate internal control over financial reporting (as defined in Rule 13a&#x2014;15(f) under the Exchange Act). Our internal control over financial reporting is a process designed under the supervision of our principal executive officer and principal financial officer to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of our financial statements for external purposes in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the U.S. Management evaluated the effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting using the criteria set forth by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (COSO) in Internal Control&#x2014;Integrated Framework (the 2013 Framework). Management, under the supervision and with the participation of the principal executive officer and principal financial officer, assessed the effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting as of </font><font style="display:inline;">December&nbsp;31, 2015</font><font style="display:inline;"> and concluded that it was not effective at a reasonable assurance level. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:3pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">As of December 31, 2015 there were material weaknesses in the Company&#x2019;s controls</font><font style="display:inline;font-family:inherit;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;font-family:inherit;">over the financial reporting process related to business combinations and accounting for significant </font><font style="display:inline;">non-routine</font><font style="display:inline;font-family:inherit;"> transactions. As a result of the limited personnel in the Company's finance and accounting group, the Company had minimal review of assumptions used and conclusions reached by third-party valuation experts used in the acquisition process</font><font style="display:inline;font-family:inherit;"> and did not have an effective process for evaluating and reviewing significant non-routine transactions</font><font style="display:inline;font-family:inherit;">. &nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:inherit;">The Company is committed to remediating the control deficiencies that constituted the above material weaknesses by implementing changes to the Company's internal control over financial reporting. Management is responsible for implementing changes and improvements in the internal control over financial reporting and for remediating the control deficiencies that gave rise to the material weaknesses. </font><font style="display:inline;font-family:inherit;">To remediate the material weakness</font><font style="display:inline;font-family:inherit;">es</font><font style="display:inline;font-family:inherit;"> described above, </font><font style="display:inline;font-family:inherit;">the Company is</font><font style="display:inline;font-family:inherit;"> currently evaluating the controls and procedures we will design </font><font style="display:inline;font-family:inherit;">and put in place to address these</font><font style="display:inline;font-family:inherit;"> material weakness</font><font style="display:inline;font-family:inherit;">es</font><font style="display:inline;font-family:inherit;"> and plan to implement appropriate measures as part of this effort. These controls and procedures may include engagement of independent consultants to aid the Company in its review of future acquisitions </font><font style="display:inline;font-family:inherit;">and </font><font style="display:inline;font-family:inherit;">significant </font><font style="display:inline;font-family:inherit;">non-</font><font style="display:inline;font-family:inherit;">routine</font><font style="display:inline;font-family:inherit;"> transactions </font><font style="display:inline;font-family:inherit;">for proper accounting. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:inherit;">Any actions </font><font style="display:inline;font-family:inherit;">the Company has</font><font style="display:inline;font-family:inherit;"> ta</font><font style="display:inline;font-family:inherit;">ken or may take to remediate the</font><font style="display:inline;font-family:inherit;">s</font><font style="display:inline;font-family:inherit;">e</font><font style="display:inline;font-family:inherit;"> material weakness</font><font style="display:inline;font-family:inherit;">es</font><font style="display:inline;font-family:inherit;"> are subject to continued management review supported by testing, as well as oversight by the Audit Commit</font><font style="display:inline;font-family:inherit;">tee of our Board of Directors. Th</font><font style="display:inline;font-family:inherit;">e</font><font style="display:inline;font-family:inherit;"> Company</font><font style="display:inline;font-family:inherit;"> cannot assure, in any way, even if </font><font style="display:inline;font-family:inherit;">the Company</font><font style="display:inline;font-family:inherit;"> involve</font><font style="display:inline;font-family:inherit;">s</font><font style="display:inline;font-family:inherit;"> an independent consultant, that material weaknesses or significant deficiencies will not</font><font style="display:inline;font-family:inherit;"> occur in the future and that the Company</font><font style="display:inline;font-family:inherit;"> will be able to remediate such weaknesses or deficiencies in a timely manner, which could impair our ability to accurately and timely report our financial position, results of operations or cash flows. </font>
		</p>

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9pt;">We have audited Aegerion Pharmaceuticals, Inc.&#x2019;s internal control over financial reporting as of December 31, 2015, based on criteria established in Internal Control &#x2013; Integrated Framework issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (2013 framework) (the COSO criteria).&nbsp;&nbsp;Aegerion Pharmaceuticals, Inc.&#x2019;s management is responsible for maintaining effective internal control over financial reporting and for its assessment of the effectiveness of internal control over financial reporting included in the accompanying Management&#x2019;s Report on Internal Control over Financial Reporting.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our responsibility is to express an opinion on the company&#x2019;s internal control over financial reporting based on our audit.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9pt;">We conducted our audit in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States).&nbsp;&nbsp;Those standards require that we plan and perform the audit to obtain reasonable assurance about whether effective internal control over financial reporting was maintained in all material respects.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our audit included obtaining an understanding of internal control over financial reporting, assessing the risk that a material weakness exists, testing and evaluating the design and operating effectiveness of internal control based on the assessed risk, and performing such other procedures as we considered necessary in the circumstances.&nbsp;&nbsp;We believe that our audit provides a reasonable basis for our opinion.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9pt;">A company&#x2019;s internal control over financial reporting is a process designed to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of financial statements for external purposes in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles.&nbsp;&nbsp;A company&#x2019;s internal control over financial reporting includes those policies and procedures that (1) pertain to the maintenance of records that, in reasonable detail, accurately and fairly reflect the transactions and dispositions of the assets of the company; (2) provide reasonable assurance that transactions are recorded as necessary to permit preparation of financial statements in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles, and that receipts and expenditures of the company are being made only in accordance with authorizations of management and directors of the company; and (3) provide reasonable assurance regarding prevention or timely detection of unauthorized acquisition, use, or disposition of the company&#x2019;s assets that could have a material effect on the financial statements.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9pt;">Because of its inherent limitations, internal control over financial reporting may not prevent or detect misstatements.&nbsp;&nbsp;Also, projections of any evaluation of effectiveness to future periods are subject to the risk that controls may become inadequate because of changes in conditions, or that the degree of compliance with the policies or procedures may deteriorate.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9pt;">A material weakness is a deficiency, or combination of deficiencies, in internal control over financial reporting, such that there is a reasonable possibility that a material misstatement of the company&#x2019;s annual or interim financial statements will not be prevented or detected on a timely basis. The following material weaknesses have been identified and included in management&#x2019;s assessment. Management has identified material weaknesses in controls related to the accounting for business combinations and the controls related to the accounting for significant non-routine transactions. We also have audited, in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States), the consolidated balance sheets of Aegerion Pharmaceuticals, Inc. as of December 31, 2015 and 2014 and the related consolidated statements of operations, comprehensive loss, stockholders&#x2019; equity and cash flows for each of the three years in the per</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:9pt;">iod ended December 31, 2015. The</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:9pt;">s</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:9pt;">e</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:9pt;"> material weakness</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:9pt;">es were</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:9pt;"> considered in determining the nature, timing and extent of audit tests applied in our audit of the 2015 consolidated financial statements, and this report does not affect our report dated March </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:9pt;">15</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:9pt;">, 2016, which expressed an unqualified opinion on those financial statements and included an explanatory paragraph regarding Aegerion Pharmaceuticals, Inc.&#x2019;s ability to continue as a going concern. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9pt;">In our opinion, because of the effect</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:9pt;">s</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:9pt;"> of the material weaknesses described above on the achievement of the objectives of the control criteria, Aegerion Pharmaceuticals, Inc. has not maintained effective internal control over financial reporting as of December 31, 2015, based on the COSO criteria.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:right;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9pt;">/s/ Ernst &amp; Young LLP</font>
		</p>
